_comment: R-164 (CL-BUG-134): a `super` call outside a constructor.
`super` emits no opcodes -- the constructor args are already on the stack --
but every tier's stack lowering pushes a stackMap slot for it anyway:
+1 model, +0 physical. On the SOURCE path that is invisible, because the
constructor is not lowered to script at all. Via `--ir` it is reachable, and
every subsequent PICK/ROLL depth is off by one.
Measured on this file against the same file with the `super` binding deleted,
through the Go tier (all six agree byte for byte):
with super     0000 53 7a 53 7a a0 7777    PUSH 3; OP_ROLL, twice
Three physical items are on the stack at that point, so a depth-3 roll
addresses a fourth that does not exist. The model and the machine disagree,
and the script is wrong in a way nothing downstream can notice.
`super` outside a constructor is not a program any of the nine frontends
produces -- a scan of all 114 checked-in IR files found 110 `super` calls and
every one of them is in a constructor -- so the loader refuses the shape
rather than inventing a physical push for a call that has no runtime meaning.
Same trust-boundary rule as the add_output arity check (R-126).
